claims.text: Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The reported 13.5% terminal strain for HfZrTiTa0.53 is a tensile strain.
The reported baseline properties were measured at room temperature and approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
Introducing approximately 0.5 at% oxygen during melting and rapidly quenching HfZrTiTa0.53 will produce nanoscale oxide precipitates at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary oxides may form transient intergranular films.
The proposed nano-oxides will blunt crack initiation during tensile loading.
The proposed nano-oxides will impede intergranular crack propagation.
The proposed modification will enhance grain-boundary sliding.
Crack blunting, impeded intergranular propagation, and enhanced grain-boundary sliding will delay catastrophic tensile failure.
Oxygen doping and rapid quenching will increase uniform tensile elongation to greater than 20%.
The modified alloy will retain a yield strength of at least approximately 786 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain approximately 1314 MPa compressive strength.
The modified alloy will maintain impact-triggered chemical-energy release at or above the undoped baseline.
The predicted mechanical response applies at approximately 25°C and a strain rate near 10^-3 s^-1 in tension and compression.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is alternately treated as terminal tensile strain, strain at failure, and the baseline uniform elongation. Total/terminal strain and uniform elongation are distinct tensile metrics, so using 13.5% as the uniform-elongation baseline is internally inconsistent.
